note: WV Roofing concept range, v2: the eight looks. They drive the swatches, the in-browser quick previews and the photo-real prompts, and never produce quantities or prices. The real manufacturers' products behind them, with their specifications for material quantities, are kept on the server only (serverlib/wvroofing/products.json). Hex values are estimates from manufacturer imagery - check against real samples before launch.

visuals.name: Natural Spanish slate
visuals.ridge: Dark grey ridge, mortar-bedded or dry-fix
visuals.suits: Victorian and Edwardian terraces, villas and period semis
visuals.summary: The classic Merseyside roof: thin blue-black slates in fine, straight courses. Natural stone that typically lasts for generations, at a fraction of the price of Welsh slate.

prompt.profile: thin, flat rectangular slates with crisp straight edges and a fine riven surface
prompt.colourWords: blue-black with very subtle grey variation from slate to slate
prompt.bond: double-lap in broken bond (each course offset by half a slate)
prompt.extra: Slates are thin: no chunky leading edges and no curved profile.

visuals.name: Welsh slate
visuals.suits: Conservation areas and like-for-like replacement of original Welsh slate
visuals.summary: The original Victorian roof, quarried in North Wales. A distinctive purple-grey 'heather blue' that weathers beautifully - the premium like-for-like choice for period homes.

prompt.profile: thin, very flat rectangular slates with fine riven surfaces and sharp straight edges
prompt.colourWords: heather blue: a soft purple-grey with gentle natural variation between slates
prompt.bond: double-lap in broken bond (each course offset by half a slate)
prompt.extra: The colour must read as purple-grey, not black.

visuals.name: Slate-effect interlocking tile
visuals.suits: 1960s-2000s homes, new builds and non-conservation terraces
visuals.summary: The look of small slates at the cost of a concrete tile. A slim 'false joint' down each tile makes it read as slate from the street - quick to fit and hard-wearing.

prompt.profile: flat tiles with a thin leading edge and a vertical false joint down each tile so they read as small slates
prompt.colourWords: smooth mid grey, very even in colour
prompt.bond: in broken bond with neat straight courses
prompt.extra: Uniform, machine-made look; keep the courses crisp.

visuals.name: Flat interlocking tile
visuals.summary: A clean, contemporary flat tile with bold horizontal shadow lines. A deep chocolate brown that suits brick houses and bungalows across Upton, Moreton and Maghull.

prompt.profile: large, flat tiles with a thick square leading edge that casts a bold horizontal shadow line under every course
prompt.colourWords: smooth dark chocolate brown, even in colour
prompt.bond: in broken bond with strong, straight horizontal courses
prompt.extra: Emphasise the clean horizontal shadow lines of this modern tile.

visuals.name: Clay plain tile
visuals.ridge: Red clay half-round or angle ridge
visuals.suits: Edwardian and 1930s hipped semis, Arts & Crafts houses
visuals.summary: Small, cambered clay tiles in dense courses - the traditional English roof. Warm red tones with natural variation, and the finest texture of any option here.

prompt.profile: small rectangular cambered tiles laid double-lap in dense courses, giving a fine, textured surface
prompt.colourWords: classic warm red with natural tonal variation from tile to tile
prompt.finish: a smooth to lightly sanded clay finish
prompt.bond: in broken bond with small, closely spaced courses
prompt.extra: Tiles are small (about 265 by 165 mm), so show many fine courses; no large interlocking tiles.

visuals.name: Double Roman tile
visuals.summary: A robust interlocking tile with two strong rolls per tile, giving bold vertical ribs down the roof. A deep antique red that sits well on brick semis.

prompt.material: Double Roman interlocking concrete roof tiles
prompt.profile: tiles with two rounded rolls each and a flat pan between them, forming continuous vertical ribs down the roof
prompt.colourWords: deep antique red, slightly weathered, with subtle variation
prompt.bond: in straight bond, rolls lined up from eaves to ridge
prompt.extra: The vertical roll pattern must be clearly visible.

visuals.name: Clay pantile
visuals.suits: Cottages, extensions, garages and some new builds
visuals.summary: The warm, wavy roof of rural England and the Mediterranean. Deep S-shaped rolls create strong shadows and a lot of character.

prompt.profile: a pronounced S-shaped wave forming continuous vertical rolls down the roof, with deep shadows between rolls
prompt.colourWords: warm natural terracotta with gentle tonal variation
prompt.bond: in straight bond, rolls aligned from course to course
prompt.extra: Make the wavy S-profile obvious; do not render flat tiles.

visuals.name: Small-format granular tile
visuals.suits: 1930s-60s semis already re-roofed in concrete tile
visuals.summary: The everyday Wirral re-roof: a neat, small-format concrete tile with a sandy granular face that looks like plain tiles from the pavement. Great value and quick to fit.

prompt.profile: neat, small tiles with a slight roll and a fine sandy granular surface, reading like plain tiles from the street
prompt.colourWords: tawny brown with a warm sandy tone and slight variation
prompt.bond: in straight bond with regular courses
prompt.extra: Keep the surface finely textured rather than glossy.
